chapter: Brass bands, Eddie Miller and band stories
title: Anton Lada, the Louisiana Five and Tony Parenti
summary: Discussion of Anton Lada, Yellow Nunez and the Louisiana Five at the Tokyo Club, and Brownlee's years of working day and night while music was an avocation.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Before we got in here, you mentioned Anton Lada too.

Oh yes, Anton Lada and Yellow Nunez. I'm trying to think of the – Anton Lada played drums, didn't he? Well I'm trying to think who the piano player was. Was it one of the Christian Broad Boys? Not that I know.
There was somebody called Joe Calway or something that played with Anton Lada one time.
Well they played at the Tokyo on 45th Off-Broadway there, the Tokyo Club. They had a right nice – Louisiana Five they called themselves. Yes, I remember now, Louisiana Five.
Were many of the guys in it from New Orleans?

Yes, there were three or four of them from New Orleans. But just like I say, I'm the world's voice on remembering all the names. If you mention a name, maybe I can give you his life history. But just to think of his name at a time like this, to broach me with something, why, to ask me to – I'd have to go in a corner in a dark room maybe for about two or three months to sit down and write all these memoirs. But if you have somebody with you to – like you reminded me of some people – speaking of Tony Perenti, for instance, Tony was a very fine person. I always liked Tony, and no doubt he'd remember me. Tony was playing in the profession of music when I was just using it as an avocation. One time there we really were on the go. I don't know how I lived up on it. I guess I worked day and night for about eight years. And that's a pretty hard thing to do. And brother, if you don't live right, you'd never make it.
